name: ahasend
label: AhaSend
note: AhaSend's v2 transactional email API behind one bearer key. The v1 API used a different credential and is not this address.

name: brevo
label: Brevo
note: Brevo's v3 API, which reads the key from its own api-key header rather than Authorization, and covers transactional email, contacts and campaigns with one key. Brevo's SMTP relay is a separate credential and does not pass this address.

name: customerio
label: Customer.io
note: Customer.io's App API on the US region, which reads campaigns, transactional messages and metrics. The Track API that receives events is a different host and authenticates with a site ID and key pair, so it is not reachable here; an EU account is the customerio-eu entry.

name: customerio-eu
label: Customer.io (EU)
note: Customer.io's App API on the EU region. A key issued in a US workspace does not resolve here, and the Track API remains a separate host and credential.

name: forwardemail
label: Forward Email
note: Forward Email's API, which reads the token as the HTTP Basic username with an empty password, which is what we send. Mail relayed through its SMTP and IMAP servers uses a mailbox password rather than this key and does not pass here.

name: loops
label: Loops
note: Loops' API for contacts, transactional email and events; call it as /gw/loops/api/v1/transactional. One bearer key covers the whole API.

name: mailersend
label: MailerSend
note: MailerSend's v1 API for email, SMS and templates behind one bearer token. Mail sent through MailerSend's SMTP relay uses a separate username and password and never passes this address.

name: mailgun
label: Mailgun
note: Mailgun's US region. It authenticates as HTTP Basic with the username api and the key as the password, which is what we send. A domain created in Mailgun's EU region answers at api.eu.mailgun.net and is the mailgun-eu entry.

name: mailgun-eu
label: Mailgun (EU)
note: Mailgun's EU region, which is where a domain created under EU data residency lives. A domain created in the US region is not visible here and is the mailgun entry.

name: postmark
label: Postmark
note: Postmark's transactional email API with a server token, which Postmark reads from X-Postmark-Server-Token. An account-level token is read from a different header and is the postmark-account entry.

name: postmark-account
label: Postmark (account token)
note: Postmark's account-level endpoints — servers, domains, sender signatures — which read X-Postmark-Account-Token. Sending a message needs a server token instead and is the postmark entry.

name: resend
label: Resend
note: Resend's email API. One bearer key covers sending, domains and audiences.

name: sendgrid
label: SendGrid
note: SendGrid's v3 API; call it as /gw/sendgrid/v3/mail/send. SendGrid's EU data residency uses a different host and needs an upstream naming it.

name: sparkpost
label: SparkPost
note: SparkPost's US API, which reads the key as the whole Authorization header with no scheme word in front of it. An EU account answers at api.eu.sparkpost.com and is the sparkpost-eu entry.

name: sparkpost-eu
label: SparkPost (EU)
note: SparkPost's EU API. A key issued on the US account does not resolve here.
